title: Requests wait for a free database session
summary: A fictional connection pool has no available sessions, and requests stall during a traffic spike.
signals: connection pool exhausted checkout timeout slow requests sessions occupied concurrency spike
steps: Check the number of active and idle sessions alongside the application's pool limit.
Look for work that holds a session longer than expected, then release connections promptly.
Reassess pool size and workload capacity before increasing either limit.

title: A TLS certificate does not match the database host
summary: A fictional client rejects the encrypted connection because the hostname and certificate do not agree.
signals: TLS handshake certificate hostname mismatch SSL verify connection
steps: Compare the configured hostname with the service's published endpoint.
Check the client trust store and certificate chain without disabling certificate validation.
Retry with the correct DNS name and verify the resulting connection.

title: A managed identity is rejected at sign-in
summary: A fictional workload cannot sign in after its user-assigned identity is changed.
signals: authentication login failed Entra managed identity principal role token permission denied
steps: Confirm the intended identity is attached to the application and selected by client ID.
Check the token audience and the database principal mapped to that identity.
Verify the principal has only the required database and model permissions.

title: An upstream service asks clients to slow down
summary: A fictional dependency responds with a rate-limit error during a burst of requests.
signals: 429 throttling retry after too many requests quota burst
steps: Inspect the dependency's rate-limit response and retry guidance.
Reduce concurrent calls and use bounded backoff where the operation can safely be retried.
Review usage and capacity before requesting a limit change.

title: A new release does not pass its health check
summary: A fictional deployment completes, but the application endpoint remains unhealthy.
signals: 502 bad gateway deploy release health probe startup port listener
steps: Compare the configured health path and listener port with the application's actual settings.
Review startup logs for a missing setting or a process that exited.
Test the health endpoint again after making a targeted correction.

title: The service name cannot be resolved
summary: A fictional client cannot turn a service hostname into an address.
signals: DNS lookup failed name resolution hostname network endpoint
steps: Check the endpoint name for spelling mistakes and unexpected suffixes.
Inspect DNS resolution from the same network as the affected workload.
Compare public and private endpoint configuration before changing network rules.

title: An idle connection closes before it is reused
summary: A fictional application sees intermittent connection failures after long quiet periods.
signals: idle connection dropped reset broken pipe reuse socket timeout
steps: Compare connection idle times with the timeouts along the network path.
Configure the client pool to retire or validate idle connections appropriately.
Observe a fresh connection after the workload has been idle.

title: A query becomes slow as the collection grows
summary: A fictional query scans more records than expected after the dataset grows.
signals: slow SQL query execution plan scan index latency database performance
steps: Capture the query plan and identify the expensive operation.
Compare existing indexes with the predicates and ordering used by the query.
Measure the effect of a reviewed change using representative synthetic data.

title: The first request after inactivity is slow
summary: A fictional app takes longer to respond while a new instance starts.
signals: cold start startup latency first request after idle warm instance
steps: Separate startup time from time spent in external dependencies.
Inspect initialization work and remove unnecessary blocking operations.
Compare the result with the hosting plan's warm-instance settings.

title: An instance restarts under memory pressure
summary: A fictional application repeatedly restarts while processing larger workloads.
signals: memory out of memory OOM restart heap process killed load
steps: Correlate restarts with memory use, request volume, and deployment changes.
Check whether buffers, caches, or concurrent work grow without a bound.
Reduce pressure or choose sufficient capacity, then observe the instance.

title: Expected request telemetry is missing
summary: A fictional dashboard shows fewer application events than expected.
signals: logs traces telemetry missing monitoring sampling instrumentation
steps: Confirm the application is configured to send telemetry to the intended destination.
Inspect sampling, filtering, and ingestion delays before changing instrumentation.
Send a synthetic request and trace it through the expected pipeline.

title: Network policy blocks a database connection
summary: A fictional workload times out because its network path is not permitted.
signals: firewall denied network access connection timeout outbound address private endpoint
steps: Identify the workload's actual network path and destination.
Review the smallest approved network rule or private connectivity option.
Test reachability and authentication separately; network access alone does not grant database access.

title: A cached response shows old information
summary: A fictional client keeps seeing an earlier response after a record changes.
signals: cache stale old data invalidation TTL response
steps: Identify each cache between the data source and the client.
Check expiration and invalidation behavior for the affected entry.
Verify a new synthetic update reaches the client after the change.

title: A workload runs short of temporary storage
summary: A fictional process cannot write a temporary file because its available space is low.
signals: disk full temporary storage no space write file
steps: Measure temporary storage use and identify the files responsible.
Review retention and cleanup behavior without removing unrelated files.
Bound temporary output and validate the workload with adequate capacity.
